GraceChangeDesignContext.NormativeStatus: non-normative; spec.xml wins on every conflict
GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
M1.3 is intentionally decomposed rather than implemented as one milestone-sized change. Tabs, history, downloads, cookies, request policy/adblock, diagnostics and search have different authority models, failure modes and persistence owners, so one approved bundle would make scope review and rollback unnecessarily broad.
This first slice chooses tabs and history because both can be implemented entirely above the existing M1.2 provider boundary and therefore prove the browser-service composition model without reopening CEF or network callbacks.
New service APIs start as experimental 0.1. M1.1/M1.2 stable browser contracts are already proven; M1.3 should not manufacture stable v1 service APIs before shell and real service consumers have exercised them.
Current NavigationCommittedEvent already carries PageId, NavigationId, URL and DocumentRevision, while PageReadyEvent carries title for the same page revision. Initial history can therefore record the committed fact and enrich title later without changing the stable navigation event.

Alternatives.Alternative: Implement every M1.3 browser service in one bundle. Rejected because the services are independently replaceable and do not form one indivisible implementation claim.
Declare browser.tabs and browser.history stable v1 immediately. Rejected because no shell or long-lived external consumer has yet provided compatibility evidence.
Let the tabs service own PageId lifecycle and close pages automatically. Rejected because tab membership is presentation/product state, whereas PageId is an engine resource with separate authority.
Treat Chromium back/forward state or the event journal as durable history. Rejected because engine recovery state, event transport and product history have different ownership and deletion semantics.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: C-BROWSER-DOWNLOADS-COOKIES-SERVICES-20260901 will define product download metadata/artifact policy and cookie inspection/policy above M1.2 engine primitives.
C-BROWSER-REQUEST-POLICY-ADBLOCK-20260901 will separately govern the provider-to-policy callback seam, bounded asynchronous decision path, recursion protection and degraded fail-open behavior.
C-BROWSER-DIAGNOSTICS-SEARCH-SERVICES-20260901 will govern bounded diagnostics without raw CDP escape and replaceable query-to-search-target providers.
C-BROWSER-SERVICES-S3-CLOSURE-20260901 will compose all completed M1.3 services against the real provider, finish the permanent S3 proving slice and only then permit M1.3 to become Done.
Workspace ownership, final tab presentation and synchronization with Worldline Shell remain M1.4/M1.5 concerns.

Scenarios.Scenario: A consumer creates a real PageId through browser.page, asks the tabs service to reference it as a new TabId, navigates through browser.navigate, and the history service durably records the committed NavigationId. Restarting history restores the record; removing the tab leaves the PageId alive.
The same committed event is delivered twice after subscriber restart. History recognizes one logical NavigationId and stores one entry.
Tabs service crashes while the browser provider remains healthy. Direct PageId navigation continues; after restart tabs reconstruct only their own persisted projection.
A page is closed independently through browser.page. Tabs reconcile the stale reference without treating their prior membership as authority to recreate the page.
